title: Maximal Cohen--Macaulay slice of a scheme groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], meaning that all its structure morphisms are over $S$. Put $G=U\times_{\Delta_{U/S},\,U\times_SU,\,(s,t)}R$, with its morphism $G\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A morphism is Cohen--Macaulay if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and every local ring of every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume $s,t$ are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $u\in U$ be a finite type point, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exist an affine scheme $B$, a locally finitely presented immersion $g:B\to U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $b\in B$ mapping to $u$, with $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(b)$ an isomorphism, such that $h=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:B\times_{g,U,t}R\to U$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation. For the point $x=(b,e(u))$ in the fibre $h^{-1}(u)$, one has $\dim_x h^{-1}(u)=\dim G_u$. Here $G_u=G\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$, dimension at a point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], and $\dim G_u$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets of $G_u$.

source.place: Tag 04MZ (lemma-max-slice), conclusions (1)--(4) and (6), with Tag 04MY (situation-slice); the immersion identifies the residue fields and hence identifies the fibre in (6) with the fibre of h.

proof.text: Write $F_u=s^{-1}(u)$ and $d=\dim_{e(u)}F_u$. At $e(u)$ choose affine source and target neighbourhoods with a finite presentation, as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Applying [lem-trf-affine-fibre-point-dimension] to $s$ and these neighbourhoods gives that $d$ is a finite nonnegative integer. The same affine calculation, $\kappa(v)\otimes_A A[z]/(f)=\kappa(v)[z]/(\bar f)$, at each point of each fibre shows that every fibre of a locally finitely presented morphism is locally of finite type over its residue field.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, first paragraph: finiteness of the induction parameter; affine fibre calculation

proof.text: The finite-type-point characterization gives an affine open $V\subset U$ in which $u$ is closed. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is a closed immersion into $V$ followed by an open immersion. Its base change by $t:F_u\to U$ identifies $G_u\to F_u$ as an immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] and composition of locally finite type maps, $G_u$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(u)$. On test schemes its arrows are loops at $u$, so the groupoid laws give it a group structure. Regard it as its actual representable algebraic space. Etale charts are locally finitely presented, hence locally of finite type, so the chartwise hypothesis of [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-constant-local-dimension] holds. That node gives $\dim_{e(u)}G_u=\sup_{z\in G_u}\dim_zG_u$. The identity atlas and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] identify this supremum with the topological dimension $a=\dim G_u$ used here.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, preceding optimality paragraph; Tag 04LU, group case (existing algebraic-space dimension node specialized to schemes)

proof.text: For completeness the immersion in step 2 implies $a\le d$ without a dimension theorem about local rings. Factor it as a closed subspace of an open $O\subset F_u$ containing $e(u)$. In any neighbourhood $N$ of $e(u)$ in $F_u$, a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $G_u\cap N$ is a chain of closed subsets of $O\cap N$. Hence $\dim(G_u\cap N)\le\dim(O\cap N)\le\dim N$, the last inequality being [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. Taking a neighbourhood $N$ attaining $d$ gives $a=\dim_{e(u)}G_u\le d$ by the definition of local dimension. In particular $a$ is also a nonnegative integer, since the identity belongs to $G_u$.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, preceding optimality paragraph: elementary chain comparison for the locally closed stabilizer

proof.text: We will use the following direct consequence of the cited statements. Arbitrary base change preserves a Cohen--Macaulay locally finitely presented morphism: on affine charts finite presentation is preserved by tensoring, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; flatness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Each new fibre is the old fibre extended along its residue-field map by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change]. The old fibres are locally finite type by step 1, so the FIRST paragraph of [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] shows their extended local rings are Cohen--Macaulay. This uses no Noetherian hypothesis on either base scheme.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, use of Tag 04MV; base change checked from affine finite presentations, flat base change, and field extension of fibres

proof.text: For any $g:B\to U$ put $H_g=B\times_{g,U,t}R$ and $R_B=H_g\times_{s\operatorname{pr}_R,U,g}B$. The source $s_B:R_B\to B$ (last projection) is the base change of $h_g=s\operatorname{pr}_R:H_g\to U$; the target is isomorphic to it by $(b_0,r,b_1)\mapsto(b_1,i(r),b_0)$. Thus when $h_g$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented so are both restricted projections, by step 4. On test schemes loops at $b\in B$ are exactly loops at $g(b)$ with the specified object $b$; consequently the restricted stabilizer is $B\times_U G$. In particular its fibre at $b$ is $G_{g(b)}\times_{\kappa(g(b))}\kappa(b)$. Also $s_B^{-1}(b)=h_g^{-1}(g(b))\times_{\kappa(g(b))}\kappa(b)$ by the fibre-of-base-change statement. These identifications send the restricted identity to $(b,e(g(b)))$.

source.place: Tag 04MY (situation-slice), Tag 04MV (lemma-restrict-property): explicit fibre products and inverse

proof.text: Use strong induction on the integer $d$ for all groupoids and finite type points in the statement, proving the stated conclusion together with the extra assertion that the two restricted projections are Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented. Steps 1--3 apply to every such input. If $d=a$, choose any affine open neighbourhood $B$ of $u$, with $b=u$. Its inclusion is an immersion and identifies residue fields. Open immersions are locally finitely presented: on affine neighbourhoods a principal open is $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ with $A_f=A[z]/(fz-1)$. The source $H_g$ is the open subscheme $t^{-1}(B)$ of $R$, so $h_g$ is the restriction of $s$, and its local rings and fibre local rings agree with those of $s$. Hence it is Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented. Step 5 proves the extra assertion. Its fibre at $u$ is an open neighbourhood of $e(u)$ in $F_u$, so [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] gives the required dimension $d=a$. This includes $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, induction and equality case; open restrictions made explicit

proof.text: If $d>a$, apply [lem-sfb-cm-groupoid-hypersurface-slice] to the given groupoid and $u$. It supplies an affine $B_0$, a locally finitely presented immersion $g_0:B_0\to U$, and $b_0$ over $u$ with the same residue field. Its saturation $h_0$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $(b_0,e(u))$ and the restricted source fibre has dimension $d-1$ at its identity. Since $s,t$ are flat and locally finitely presented and $g_0$ is locally finitely presented, [lem-sfb-groupoid-cm-locus-descent] applies and gives an open $W\subset B_0$ containing $b_0$, with $h_0$ Cohen--Macaulay on the entire inverse image of $W$.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, strict case: Tag 0461 followed by Tag 047W(5)

proof.text: Choose an affine open $B_1\subset W$ containing $b_0$ and put $b_1=b_0$. The immersion $g_1:B_1\to U$ is the composite of this open inclusion and $g_0$, so remains an immersion and locally finitely presented, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), the local presentation of an open inclusion from step 6, and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. The saturation $h_1$ is a source-open restriction of $h_0|_{p^{-1}(W)}$, so remains Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented. Step 5 gives Cohen--Macaulay locally finitely presented restricted projections. The restricted source fibre is an open neighbourhood of the identity in the previous restricted fibre, so still has local dimension $d-1$. Finally $b_1$ is a finite type point: choose the affine $V\subset U$ of step 2; the immersion makes $b_1$ closed in $g_1^{-1}(V)$, and then in an affine neighbourhood inside this open. The finite-type-point characterization applies with the identity residue-field extension.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, shrinking the first slice, verifying the induction hypotheses

proof.text: The restricted groupoid over $B_1$ and $b_1$ now meets every hypothesis of the induction claim, with parameter $d-1<d$. Apply it to obtain an affine $C$, a locally finitely presented immersion $j:C\to B_1$, and $c\in C$ over $b_1$ with identical residue field. The saturation $h_{C/B_1}$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented; the twice restricted source fibre at its identity has dimension equal to the stabilizer fibre of the groupoid over $B_1$ at $b_1$. By step 5 and $\kappa(b_1)=\kappa(u)$ that stabilizer fibre is canonically $G_u$. The twice restricted projections also satisfy the extra assertion of the induction claim.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, application of the induction hypothesis

proof.text: Set $g=g_1\circ j:C\to U$. Composition of immersions and of locally finitely presented morphisms gives the required type of $g$; its residue-field map at $c$ is the composite of two isomorphisms. The two saturation maps $h_1$ and $h_{C/B_1}$ are Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented. Applying [lem-sfb-cm-groupoid-double-restriction] gives that $h_C=s\operatorname{pr}_R:C\times_{g,U,t}R\to U$ has these properties as well. This application requires no global surjectivity for $h_1$. Step 5 gives the extra assertion for the restriction directly to $C$.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, final paragraph: composite immersion and Tag 04MX

proof.text: Associating fibre products identifies the twice restricted arrow scheme with $C\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}C$: on test schemes both consist of $(c_0,r,c_1)$ with $t(r)=g(c_0)$ and $s(r)=g(c_1)$; the intermediate objects are forced to be $j(c_0),j(c_1)$. This isomorphism preserves source, target and identity. By step 5 its source fibre at $c$ is $h_C^{-1}(u)\times_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(c)$. The map $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(c)$ is an isomorphism, so projection identifies this fibre with $h_C^{-1}(u)$, taking its identity to $x=(c,e(u))$. Step 9 therefore gives $\dim_x h_C^{-1}(u)=\dim G_u$. Taking $B=C$ and $b=c$ completes the induction and the proof.

source.place: Tag 04MZ, clauses (5),(6) under composition; explicit identifications from Tag 04MY
